policy: Fixed stack margins qualify development-toolchain code generation, not the minimum supported language/library API level. Older supported compilers may need larger stacks in debug builds. Only workspace entries are skipped by the MSRV workspace test command; development-toolchain workspace runs use no exclusions.

tests.reason: Cold document schema compilation and local validation on a 256 KiB thread stack; Rust 1.88 debug code generation exceeds this margin.

Prepares value contracts whose patterns nest to the default pattern_depth, and checks values against them, on a 256 KiB thread stack. Release builds need at most 96 KiB; unoptimized pattern compilation needs up to 1 MiB, so debug runs ignore it on every host and tools/verify.py runs it in release builds.

Prepares recursive contracts through every applicator family, unevaluated keywords included, and checks and explains values as deep as the default evaluation depth admits, on a 256 KiB thread stack. Unoptimized evaluation frames exceed this margin, so debug runs ignore it on every host and tools/verify.py runs it in release builds.

Prepares the longest unevaluated annotation walk of each kind the walk limit admits, below enclosing schemas, on a 256 KiB thread stack with a fifth of it already in use. Release builds still prepare each with up to 57 KiB already in use on Windows, 91 KiB on Linux and 107 KiB on macOS; unoptimized compilation frames exceed this margin, so debug runs ignore it on every host and tools/verify.py runs it in release builds.
